ana: quick update — we finished the rollout of adaptive-coalescer v2 to all short-chat clusters (seq <= 128).

ana: TL;DR: p99 latency down ~14% for chat workloads, median latency unchanged, and token cost down ~18% on average across the canary traffic mix.

jordan: awesome. can you paste the canary numbers?

ana: canary window (2h): baseline p99 = 256ms -> v2 p99 = 220ms, p50 = 42ms -> 41ms. throughput at 95th percentile improved ~9%. cost/sample (measured by token compute units) -18%.

mike: which models were included?

ana: initially rolled on: rwd-small-chat-v1, rwd-medium-chat-v1, and two open models we host (ggml-chat-7b, llama-mini-chat). We excluded long-seq and streaming-only routes.

sara: what changed under the hood?

ana: short summary — we switched from fixed microbatch windows to an adaptive coalescer that dynamically merges concurrent requests if they share prefix-KV compatibility and estimated tail risk is low. It also applies a short straggler-suppression timer (30ms) and opportunistic priority lanes for interactive traffic.

ana: small config snippet we flipped:
```
coalescer.mode = "adaptive"
coalescer.max_wait_ms = 30
coalescer.prefix_compatibility = true
```

eva: any regressions or gotchas?

ana: two things we watched: (1) tail-burst patterns on a small customer caused a transient p95 spike during canary #2 — fixed by tightening the priority lane cutoff. (2) We saw ~2% increase in memory pressure on some older nodes; autoscaler drained a couple hosts and replaced them. No data loss.

deploy-bot: canary: adaptive-coalescer-v2 promoted to default in region-us-west-2 at 2026-11-03T02:12:47Z :white_check_mark:

jordan: nice. ops playbook? where to look for alerts?

ana: dashboards: https://dashboards.redwood.com/d/abc123/adaptive-coalescer-v2-metrics 
runbook: https://wiki.redwood.com/runbooks/coalescer-adaptive-v2 
alerting: new alerts added -> coalescer.queue-length.p95 and coalescer.tail-regressions.rate.

mike: do customers need to change anything?

ana: no API changes. There is a performance policy change though: default batching policy for seq<=128 is now "latency-cost-balanced". Teams who rely on absolute minimal tail latency can opt out by setting route config: `batching.policy = "latency-first"`.

sara: could we add a flag to the dashboard to visualize how many routes are opted out?

ana: good idea — filing a tiny follow-up ticket. thanks to infra + runtime + sres for quick turn. :party:

eva: monitoring will keep an extra eye on p99 for 24h, tagging any +5% regressions.

jordan: huge win. can we share a short note for #announcements tomorrow?

ana: yes, will draft and drop here in the morning.

mike: reassigning a few follow-ups: ticket #4928 (opt-out flag dashboard), #4930 (memory-pressure mitigations for old nodes), #4931 (post-rollout perf regression checklist).

ana: ok closing thread — ping me if you see anything odd.
